info.title: FlexStore Storefront API
info.description:
The customer-facing API behind a FlexStore shop: catalog, cart, checkout, orders and accounts.

Everything a shopper can do on the storefront is available here, which makes it the API to build a mobile app on.

get.description: Saved addresses, newest first, with the default flagged.

post.description: Saves a new address to the customer's address book. Required fields vary by country: a US address needs a state and ZIP, others may not.

patch.description: Partial update: omitted fields keep their current value.

delete.description: Removes the address. Orders already placed keep their own copy.

post.description: Makes this the address preselected at checkout. Any previous default is cleared.

get.description: Products the customer is comparing, as catalog cards.

delete.description: Empties the comparison list and returns it.

put.summary: Add a product to the comparison list
put.description: Adds a product. Adding one already on the list is a no-op.

delete.summary: Remove a product from the comparison list
delete.description: Removes a product. Removing one that is absent is a no-op.

get.description: Digital files the customer has bought, across all paid orders.
Streams the purchased file itself, not JSON. Each successful call counts against the download limit, and an expired or revoked grant is refused.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by fulfillment status, or `cancelled` for canceled orders.

get.description: The customer’s orders, newest first, each with a short item preview.
One order in full: line items, totals, addresses, shipment and payment status. Another customer's order returns 404.

post.summary: Add a past order to the cart

200.description: The cart with everything still available added.

422.description: Nothing from the order is still available.

post.description: Adds the order’s still-available items to the cart. Items that are gone or out of stock are skipped.

get.description: Returns the invoice as a PDF file, not JSON.
Call before showing a return form, to know which items and quantities can still go back.

customer_note.example: Too small, would like to send it back.

410.description: The order has no collected payment to return against.

post.description: Requests a return for delivered items. Check eligibility first to know what can still go back.

put.description: Requires the current password. Existing tokens stay valid.

get.description: The account behind the token: name, email, and whether the email is verified.

patch.description: Changing the email sends a new verification link. Omitted fields are left alone.

200.description: Account deleted and every token revoked.

delete.description: Permanently deletes the account and revokes every token. Requires the current password.

410.description: The return has moved past the point where it can be canceled.

post.description: Withdraws a return the merchant has not acted on yet.

get.description: Saved products, as catalog cards. At most 100 products are returned.

put.summary: Add a product to the wishlist
put.description: Saves a product. Saving one already on the list is a no-op.

delete.summary: Remove a product from the wishlist
delete.description: Removes a product. Removing one that is absent is a no-op.

get.summary: Get the address fields for a country

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, case insensitive.

get.description: Build the checkout address form from this rather than assuming a fixed set of fields. A US address needs a state and ZIP; many countries do not.

200.description: Which fields to show, which are required, and how to label them.

get.description: The refund, privacy or terms text. A policy the merchant has not written returns 404, and `/config` lists which ones exist so a client can hide the links it should not show.

post.description: Sends the verification link again. Returns success without sending when the address is already verified.

Send the whole query from the verification email's link. The emailed link points at the storefront, so a native client reads the values out of the deep link rather than following it. The signature is what proves the customer opened the email, and it expires with the link.

signature.description: The `signature` value from the link. It proves the link came from the store, so a token alone cannot verify an address.

403.description: The link is not valid for the authenticated account, was tampered with, or has expired.

200.description: Accepted. The response is identical whether or not the account exists.

post.description: Emails a reset link. The response is identical whether or not the account exists.
Verifies an email and password and returns a token for every other account endpoint. Repeated failures are throttled per email and IP.
Revokes only the token used for this request. Other devices stay logged in.

device_name.description: Names the token, so a customer can tell their devices apart.

post.description: Creates a customer account and returns a token, so no separate log in call is needed.

post.summary: Reset a password with a token
post.description: Sets a new password using the token from the reset email.

post.summary: Log in with a social provider

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The social provider to log in with.

post.description: Send the token the provider's SDK returned and get a FlexStore token back. The account is matched by provider account or email, and created if neither matches. Request the token for the store's own client id, not the app's, so it verifies against the merchant's credentials. A provider the merchant has not configured returns 404.

access_token.description: The token the provider's SDK returned when the customer signed in.

device_name.description: Labels the token so the customer can tell their devices apart.

get.description: Published posts, newest first.
Published posts by one author, newest first. An author with no published posts returns 404.
A published post, including its body. Drafts and future-dated posts return 404.
Active brands, alphabetical.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Defaults to the store setting. `relevance` applies only with a `query`.

get.description: Products for one brand, accepting the same filters as the shop listing.
Creates a cart when `X-Cart-Token` is missing or unknown, so the first call always succeeds. Store the returned `token`.

200.description: The cart. A new one is created when no token is sent.

delete.description: Removes every line and returns the empty cart.

get.description: Products the merchant paired with what is already in the cart.

post.summary: Add an item to the cart
post.description: Adding to a line that already exists increases its quantity. Fails validation when the requested quantity is above available stock.

product_variant_id.description: Required when the product has variants.

patch.description: Sets the quantity for a line. Sending zero removes it. Fails when the quantity exceeds available stock.

delete.summary: Remove an item from the cart
delete.description: Removes one line and returns the recalculated cart.

post.summary: Add shared items to the cart

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: The encoded item list from a share link.

200.description: The cart with the link's items added.

422.description: Nothing in the link is still available.

post.description: Adds the items encoded in a shared cart link. Unavailable items are skipped.

200.description: The category tree with product counts.

get.description: The category tree, each node carrying the number of products in it and below it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Defaults to the store setting. `relevance` applies only with a `query`.

get.description: Includes products in descendant categories.

post.description: Reserves stock and creates a payment session. Send the buyer to `redirect_url` in a web view, then poll the session endpoint when they come back. When the store has guest checkout switched off, a bearer token is required.

shipping_rate_id.description: Omit for a cart that needs no shipping.

shipping_quote_reference.description: Required for live carrier rates; copy it from the chosen shipping option.

card_token.description: Required by gateways that tokenise the card in the client.

shared_payment.description: Create a shared payment link instead of paying now. The response's `redirect_url` is the link to hand to the payer. Rejected when the merchant has checkout sharing switched off.

422.description: Validation failed, the cart is empty, stock ran out, or the gateway declined.

200.description: The cart with the discount applied.

post.description: Applies a discount code and returns the cart with recalculated totals. An invalid or ineligible code fails validation.

delete.description: Removes the applied code and returns the recalculated cart.

patch.description: Call this as the buyer fills the checkout form, debounced. It keeps the pending checkout session current, which is what puts an abandoned checkout in the merchant's recovery list and lets them email the buyer a way back. Skip it and app checkouts are invisible to recovery.

200.description: Draft saved. `coupon_removed` is true when the change invalidated the applied coupon.

post.description: Persists the buyer's choice before they place the order, so totals and the abandoned-checkout snapshot reflect it.

200.description: The cart with the selection and recalculated totals.

post.description: The gateways this buyer can pay with, filtered by the destination address and what is in the cart. Options carry the public keys an embedded or native gateway SDK needs. Send an empty body to list every gateway before an address is known.

200.description: Gateways eligible for this cart and destination.

get.description: Open this from a recovery email deep link, then store the returned `token` as the device's cart.

200.description: The abandoned cart, ready to adopt.

410.description: The checkout was completed or the link expired.

get.description: Call this when the payment web view closes. A pending session is verified with the gateway, so this is what turns a paid session into an order. The full order is included only for a signed-in buyer; guests get `order_id`.

200.description: The session, with the order once payment settles.

delete.description: Call when the buyer abandons the payment step, so held stock is released instead of waiting to expire. A session waiting on a shared payment is left running, since someone else may still be paying it.

200.description: Session canceled and reserved stock released.

get.description: For the person who was asked to pay. The session id is the capability; expiry is enforced from the session.

200.description: What is owed and how it can be paid.

410.description: Already paid, expired, or no longer shared. The body carries a `status` of `paid`, `expired`, `discount` or `inactive`.

message.example: This payment link is no longer active.

410.description: The link is no longer payable.

post.description: Pays a shared link. Reserves stock and returns a payment session to complete, the same shape as regular checkout.

The shipping methods available to the destination address, each with its price and estimated tax. Includes live carrier quotes when the merchant has a carrier connected; pass the chosen option's `quote_reference` back when submitting the checkout.

200.description: Available shipping options and the estimated tax for this destination.

get.description: Everything a client needs at start-up: store identity, available locales and currencies, and checkout switches. `policies` names the policies the merchant has written; fetch the text itself from `/policies/{policy}`.

200.description: Running sales, each with a short product preview.

get.description: Sales running now, each with a short product preview. Sales with no purchasable products are omitted.
One running sale with its products and the time it ends. A sale that has not started or has ended returns 404. At most 60 products are returned; `products_count` reports how many the sale covers.

200.description: The sale with all of its products.

get.description: The merchandising sections the merchant configured, in display order, so an app home screen can mirror the storefront. Presentation hints such as `text_align`, `autoplay` and `grayscale` may be ignored by a native client, and `icon_name` is a stable identifier to map to your own icon set. Send `X-Visitor-Id` so a recently viewed section can show this device's history.

503.description: The merchant has no newsletter provider connected.

post.description: Adds the address to the merchant’s connected newsletter provider.

post.summary: Track an order without logging in
post.description: Looks up an order by its number and the email it was placed with, for buyers who checked out without an account. Returns status and items only, never payment details.

get.description: A merchant can email a link for a balance due on an order. This is that link's data.

200.description: The outstanding balance and how to pay it.

410.description: Expired, closed, or the balance is already settled.

post.description: Starts payment for the outstanding balance and returns a session to complete.
Discards the pending payment session for a payment request. Call when the payer backs out of the payment step, so they can start again cleanly.

get.description: Also records a product view. Send `X-Visitor-Id` so repeat views from the same device are counted once; without it, nothing is recorded.
Products similar to this one, chosen by category and price. Falls back to a broader pool when the category is thin.
Approved reviews, newest first. Pending reviews are never returned.

post.description: Only a customer who bought the product and has not reviewed it yet can post. New reviews wait for approval.

content.example: Wore it all through January and it still looks new.

Currency.name: X-Currency

exchange_rate.description: Rate against the base currency. Prices are returned in the base currency, so multiply by this to display in the selected one.

redirect_url.description: Open in a web view. External for hosted gateways; an internal signed URL when no redirect is needed.

payload.description: Gateway specific fields for native or embedded flows, for example a Stripe client secret. Keys differ per provider; pass them to that provider SDK unchanged.

returnable_quantities.description: Map of order item id to the quantity still returnable.

AddressFieldRules.description: Which address fields a country requires, and what to label them. Shape varies by country.

payload.description: Gateway specific fields for native or embedded flows. Keys differ per provider.

CartItemOptions.description: Selected option values, keyed by option name.

TrackedOrderLine.description: One line of a checkout or order, in the shape every payment link and tracking response uses.

type.description: `shipment` for dispatched lines, `pending` for the rest.

TrackedOrder.description: Order status grouped by shipment, for a guest who has only the order number and email.

FlashSalePrice.description: Present when the product is in a running flash sale. Use `flash_sale_price` as the price to show and `ends_at` for a countdown.

quantity_limit.description: Units allocated to the sale, null when unlimited.

quantity_remaining.description: Null when there is no limit.

LinkTarget.description: A storefront link resolved into something a native client can navigate. Only `type` is always present; the other fields appear for the types that need them, so a `category` target carries `handle` and nothing else. Unrecognised paths come back as type `url` with the raw link, so there is always a usable fallback.

handle.description: Present for category, brand, product, flash_sale and post targets.

query.description: Present for shop targets that carried filters.

url.description: The raw link. Present only for `external` and `url` targets, where there is nothing else to navigate by.

settings.description: Section content, shaped by `type`. Text is resolved to the requested locale, images to media objects, and products and posts to full cards. Link fields are always accompanied by a resolved target: `url` by `target`, `view_all_url` by `view_all_target`, `button_url` by `button_target`, at whatever depth they appear.

content.description: The text the merchant wrote, as entered in the admin panel.

allOf.description: A product card plus the attributes a comparison table lines up side by side.
